thread:
carla_support: Heads-up — getting a spike of 500/503s from hosted inference across a few customers starting ~06:12 UTC. Customers report short lived requests failing and retries. Seeing runner containers restart.
ops_oncall: Confirmed. Alerts showing restart_count > 4 on pool-gpu-08. Killed pods with image infer-runner:v2.4 restarted automatically.
ben_infra: Pulled logs from one affected pod, looks like a cuda runtime abort then segfault in the native layer. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T06:12:34Z] runtime error: cuda runtime abort: invalid device pointer
[2026-03-17T06:12:34Z] signal SIGSEGV (segmentation fault) at 0x7f8c3b2
[2026-03-17T06:12:34Z] Backtrace (most recent call last):
  native_infer.cc:452 run_step
  runtime_loop.cc:121 kernel_launch
  ...
```
carla_support: Customer A saying it started after we rolled model variant gpt-large-ctx-8k->gpt-large-ctx-32k around 06:08. Could be context-length related.
dinesh_ml: That matches an experiment I ran earlier — KV cache paths not fully exercised for large contexts in the quantized path. Repro steps I tried locally:
1) request generation with context_size=28000
2) batch size 8, prefetched KV true
3) send multi-turn with 2 warmup calls then large prompt
Result: native crash in kv_cache->resize path.
alice.dev: I captured a container syslog and a kernel oops line on the host when the container died:
```
Mar 17 06:12:35 host-gpu-08 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:3e:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 17 06:12:35 host-gpu-08 systemd[1]: infer-runner.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```
ops_oncall: Deploy-bot reports repeated restarts and the node killed the container due to OOM on host memory (not just GPU). From node metrics: hostfree dropped ~8GB before evict.
deploy-bot: [auto] pool-gpu-08 infer-runner:v2.4 restart_count=7 -> marking for cordon until triage.
ben_infra: Quick mitigation plan:
- rollback model variant to ctx-8k for affected pool via routing policy (canary rollback)
- disable KV prefetch on pool-gpu-08 env var INFER_KV_PREFETCH=false
- reduce max_batch_size from 16->8
These should reduce memory pressure immediately.
dinesh_ml: For repro, here's a minimal curl that triggers the crash in my lab (use on staging only):
```
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-ctx-32k","input":"A"*25000,"max_tokens":512,"prefetch_kv":true,"batch_size":8}'
```
Note: requires sequence > 20k to exercise the bug.
carla_support: Customer-facing note: telling affected customers we see upstream worker crashes and are routing around affected nodes; will follow up with ETA. Filing support ticket linking this thread.
ops_oncall: Collected core dump and gdb backtrace; attaching pointer: /artifacts/core/infer-runner.3141592653.core (s3 link in triage ticket). Backtrace shows native_infer::kv_resize() -> nvmm_alloc -> cudaMallocManaged got invalid pointer returned.
ben_infra: Likely root cause: interaction between large host-managed allocations for KV cache and our quantized kernels leading to illegal device pointer references after a context resize. Could be a race on rebind to device pointers during migration between streams.
dinesh_ml: I'll reproduce with memory sanitizer build and a patched kv_resize guard. If reproduced will open PR with a fix and a unit test covering multi-warmup large-context sequences.
alice.dev: Ops note: cordon node pool-gpu-08, cordon completed. Routing policy rolled traffic off that pool at 06:24 UTC. Telemetry shows errors dropping ~70% after rollback to ctx-8k for affected customers.
carla_support: Next steps for support: share short postmortem in #incidents after we have root cause, timeline, and customer impact. For now communicate rollback and ETA for fix.
ops_oncall: ETA: reproduce & PR by EOD, hotfix roll to staging in ~3h, production rollout after verification.
carla_support: Thanks — updating customer tickets and leaving this thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
